title: Embedding vector dimensionality migration — projection, dual-indexing, and client adapter playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Context:
We are preparing to change the canonical embedding dimensionality for the primary text embedding model used by the reranking pipeline (current: 768 -> target: 1024). The change improves downstream rerank quality (NDCG/R@k) but impacts index formats, ANN search latency, storage, and client compatibility. This ticket is a playbook to migrate embeddings with minimal client breakage and predictable performance behavior.

Goals:
- Swap to 1024-dim vectors while preserving availability and latency SLOs for reranking endpoints.
- Provide client-side and server-side adapters during the migration window to avoid forced client upgrades.
- Ensure rerank quality gains are validated and monitored before full cutover.
- Limit storage and QPS cost increases via quantization and index tuning.

Options considered (summary):
1) Atomic reindex + swap: build a new index with 1024 dims, validate, then atomically swap. Simple but requires sufficient indexing capacity and has switch moment risk.
2) Dual-index router: keep old (768) and new (1024) indices and route traffic by canary rules. Gradually increase traffic to the new index while maintaining fallbacks.
3) On-the-fly projection adapter: accept 768-dim vectors and project to 1024 via a learned linear transform (A matrix) or PCA-based expansion when clients cannot upgrade immediately. Lower immediate cost but may lose some of model improvements.
4) Hybrid: route queries to both indices and merge scores (cheap for top-k candidates). Useful as a temporary quality safety net.
5) Client-enforced strict mode: for enterprise customers who choose strict type safety, reject mismatched dims with clear error codes.

Recommended approach (composed):
- Primary migration strategy: Dual-index router + background reindex (option 2) with on-the-fly projection adapter (option 3) enabled as a safety fallback.
- Rationale: Dual-index enables incremental rollout and A/B quality measurement; the adapter addresses lagging clients without blocking new deployments.

Index and API compatibility changes:
- Add index metadata fields: schema_version (string), vector_dim (int), model_id (string), created_at. All new indices must include these.
- API behavior: when a client submits a vector whose dim != index.vector_dim, return 409 with an explanatory message and headers: X-Expected-Dim, X-Index-Schema-Version. In non-strict mode, server may attempt projection or padding/truncation if configured.
- SDK changes: introduce a migration option on clients: embedClient.migrationMode = "strict" | "pad" | "project". Default for GA: "project" for 30 days, then shift default to "strict" once most clients have migrated.

Index build & storage considerations:
- Expect ~1.33x raw storage increase if changing 768->1024 at float32. Use mixed-precision storage and per-index quantization (8-bit PQ or 16-bit) to cap growth.
- Reindexing strategy: parallel reindex workers reading canonical documents, generating new embeddings, and writing to a new index name (docs_v2_1024). Keep write throttles to avoid overloading inference/IO.
- ANN tuning: for HNSW/FAISS, expect increased memory for graph/connectivity. Re-evaluate efSearch, efConstruction, and M parameters to preserve latency SLOs.

Validation and metrics (pre-cutover):
- Quality: NDCG@10 delta, Recall@K (K=1,5,10), rerank precision lift on a labeled holdout. Target: statistically significant improvement (p<0.05) vs baseline.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for rerank endpoint should remain within current SLOs (p95 increase acceptable up to +15% during reindex).
- Resource: GPU/CPU usage, index memory footprint, disk storage growth, and query throughput.
- Error rates: dimension-mismatch errors, adapter fallbacks, timeout/circuit events.

Rollout plan (detailed):
1) Prep (0-2 weeks):
   - Create new index builder jobs and deploy reindex workers in staging.
   - Implement schema_version & vector_dim in index metadata.
   - Ship SDK adapter option and server-side projection plugin behind feature flag.
   - Add dashboard panels for new metrics.
2) Canary (week 3):
   - Build a full new index in prod (docs_v2_1024) using limited write concurrency.
   - Run offline quality comparisons on holdout; collect NDCG & R@k.
   - Start 1–5% canary traffic to new index for read-only requests; measure latency and quality.
3) Ramp (week 4):
   - Increase traffic by 10–20% steps with 24–48h observation windows.
   - Disable projection adapter for canary clients to get true comparison metrics.
   - Adjust ANN tuning parameters if p95 latency regresses.
4) Full cutover (after acceptance):
   - Switch router default to new index for read traffic. Keep old index for 14 days as fallback.
   - Deprecation window: announce client SDK change and plan to require 1024 by deprecation date (30–60 days).
5) Decommission old index:
   - After 2 retention cycles and no fallbacks observed, delete old index.

Client impact and communication:
- Surface: clients may see explicit 409 dimension-mismatch errors until they upgrade. For managed SDKs, shipping migrationMode="project" will hide breakage for a limited period.
- Communication plan: staging announcement (engineering), two-week advance notice for canary, public deprecation notice for upgrade-required date, changelog and SDK release notes with migration guide.

Operational runbook (high-level):
- To start a reindex: redwoodctl embeddings reindex --source-index docs_v2 --model embed-v2 --target-index docs_v2_1024 --concurrency 8 --quantize 8bit
- To start canary routing: redwoodctl router traffic-split --route rerank-read --index docs_v2_1024 --percent 5
- To rollback routing: redwoodctl router traffic-swap --route rerank-read --index docs_v2 --force
- To inspect index metadata: redwoodctl index inspect docs_v2_1024 --fields schema_version,vector_dim,model_id

Acceptance criteria (must pass before full cutover):
- New index built and verified with schema_version and vector_dim set.
- Holdout NDCG@10 shows non-negative or net-positive change and passes statistical test.
- Rerank endpoint p95 increase <= 15% and p99 within acceptable bounds or mitigated by ANN tuning.
- No more than 0.1% of customers experience adapter fallback errors in the canary window.
- SDKs released for JS/Python/Go with migrationMode support and docs published.

Post-migration tasks:
- Update billing & capacity forecasts to reflect storage/QPS deltas.
- Add a permanent index metadata check to CI to require vector_dim on new indices.
- Conduct postmortem if rollback occurs.

Open decisions (requires PM/Infra sign-off):
- Default migrationMode after 30 days (strict vs project). Recommendation: flip to strict once 80% of active SDK clients have updated.
- Quantization defaults: 8-bit PQ vs 16-bit float for new indices. Recommend 8-bit PQ initial, with opt-out for high-precision indices.
